decision_points.question: how are records with a missing referee bias score (IAT / explicit) handled?
decision_points.why_rival: each disposes of the same unmeasured-bias records one way — median-impute, mean-impute, country-mean-impute, or drop — and an analyst picks a single disposition; none co-occur

decision_points.question: how are missing player-height values handled?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the fill/drop choice for the height covariate specifically, a separate variable from bias or position

decision_points.question: how are non-numeric placeholder / non-finite values coerced to numeric-with-missing during cleaning?
decision_points.why_rival: each is a rival recipe for turning 'NA' strings / non-finite ratios into proper numeric missing before modeling (the single 4-18 co-run reads as the same coercion slot logged twice)

decision_points.question: which referee-bias measures are included in the adjustment model?
decision_points.why_rival: include both implicit and explicit bias vs drop the implicit (meanIAT) covariate — mutually exclusive covariate sets

decision_points.question: how are model covariates standardized and their missing standardized values filled?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the z-score-and-zero-fill scaling approach for the covariate block

decision_points.question: are referee countries with too-small or missing bias-survey samples excluded?
decision_points.why_rival: settles whether unreliable-sample countries are dropped from the country-level bias measure

decision_points.question: which set of countries defines the mean used to center bias scores?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the reference group for centering; co-occurs with the exclusion step (8), so it is a distinct downstream choice, not its rival

decision_points.question: how is the country-level referee bias measure aggregated / modeled?
decision_points.why_rival: random-effect shrinkage vs collapse-and-z-standardize vs plain within-country average are three mutually exclusive ways to produce one country bias value

decision_points.question: how are standard errors / confidence intervals estimated for the main effect?
decision_points.why_rival: BCa bootstrap CI vs robust sandwich SE are rival uncertainty-quantification methods; they never co-occur

decision_points.question: what generic fallback is applied to otherwise-unhandled missing values?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the catch-all default (Unknown category or median/mean) for values no specific rule covers

decision_points.question: how are player positions categorized and how are missing / uncategorizable positions handled?
decision_points.why_rival: keep-as-Unknown-category, impute-modal, drop, drop-if-unmappable, exclude-from-viz-only, and the 6-category-with-Missing-residual scheme are alternative dispositions of missing-position records; the big three (14/30/38) never co-occur

decision_points.question: what regression model form is used for the outcome?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the estimator/specification (linear probability model with clustered SE) for the main model

decision_points.question: how are the interaction coefficients presented in the results table?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the reporting/formatting of the rater×bias interaction output

decision_points.question: how are column names sanitized before model formulas are built?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the name-cleaning step (stripping spaces) that precedes formula construction

decision_points.question: how is the analytic sample restricted to complete / relevant records?
decision_points.why_rival: restrict to non-missing raters plus single-game dyads vs restrict to non-missing values of each question's key variable — rival rules for who stays in the sample

decision_points.question: what is the scope of complete-case / listwise deletion of records with missing covariates?
decision_points.why_rival: drop-if-missing-any-adjustment-covariate vs drop-if-any-missing-value-anywhere vs drop-if-missing-any-analysis-set-covariate are nested rival scopes of the same listwise-deletion decision

decision_points.question: how are categorical variables dummy-encoded for the model?
decision_points.why_rival: settles full one-hot with no reference dropped vs the reference-dropped alternative

decision_points.question: which version / sheet of the dataset is loaded?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the data source — the pre-coded, missing-deleted crowdstorming sheet vs raw alternatives

decision_points.question: are the bias-by-rater interaction terms mean-centered before entry?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the centering of the interaction terms; co-occurs with the count decision (34), so it is a distinct construction choice

decision_points.question: how many rater×bias interaction terms enter the model as the final block?
decision_points.why_rival: a single interaction term vs both terms together — mutually exclusive final-block specifications that never co-occur

decision_points.question: how are the country-level red-card and bias tables combined?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the merge that assembles the country-level analysis table

decision_points.question: which dyads are retained based on the two raters' skin-tone agreement?
decision_points.why_rival: settles whether only exactly-matching-rater dyads are kept, a rival to averaging / keeping disagreements

decision_points.question: how is moderation of the referee-bias effect by player skin tone assessed?
decision_points.why_rival: stratified subgroup regressions plus a t-test vs a pooled dark-skin×modifier interaction vs the specific dark_skin×meanIAT interaction are rival ways to test the same moderation

decision_points.question: how is the binary dark-skin exposure variable defined?
decision_points.why_rival: recode the given light/dark category to 0/1 vs empirically choose the cutoff that maximizes the split — rival routes to the same binary; they never co-occur
